Re: Deposit Refund – Flat 2, 14 Saxby Street

I am writing to formally request a refund of the deposit, in accordance with the terms of our Assured Shorthold Tenancy Agreement dated 1 March 2023. The tenancy ended on 31 August 2026, and I returned the keys to you on that date.

As outlined in **Clause 4.1** of our agreement, the deposit of £1,450 was protected with the Deposit Protection Service (DPS) on 10 March 2023, and you were required to provide the prescribed information within 3,0 days of receiving it. I trust that this was done in a timely manner.

Under **Clause 4.3**, you may deduct from the deposit the reasonable cost of making good any damage caused by me, with fair wear and tear excepted. The check-in inventory dated 1 March 2023 recorded the living room walls as “magnolia, freshly painted, good condition.” The check-out report dated 3 September 2026 noted “light scuffing to living room walls near sofa; two picture hook holes.”

I accept that the two picture hook holes may require some touch-up, and I am willing to pay a reasonable sum for that. However, the claim of “full redecoration” and the deduction of £900 is not supported by the facts or the terms of the agreement. The condition of the walls, as described in the check-out report, does not justify such a significant deduction, especially when the damage is limited to minor scuffing and two small holes.

According to the **Deposit Scheme Rules**, any deduction must be reasonable and supported by evidence. The cost of redecoration is not a legitimate deduction unless it is directly related to damage caused by the tenant, and even then, it should be limited to the actual cost of repairs.

I therefore request that you refund the deposit in full, minus any reasonable and documented deductions for damage. I am prepared to settle the cost of the two picture hook holes at £60, as I have previously stated, and I would appreciate your confirmation of this.

Please respond in writing within 14 days of receiving this letter, in accordance with the Deposit Protection Service rules. If you are unable to do so, I will take the matter further, including contacting the DPS and potentially seeking resolution through the relevant housing authority.

Yours sincerely,  
**Ms Aisha Okafor**
